 UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R It is contended by Mr. Siddharth Dave, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners that prior to the amendment by Finance Act 20 of 2015, there were separate categories of offences included in Part-A Savita Srivastava vs Directorate Of Enforcement on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58359327/
1 and Part-B of the Schedule to the Prevention of Money- laundering Act, 2002 (for short PMLA).
The definition of the expression scheduled offence under Section 2(1)(y) of PMLA deals with 3 categories of offences namely (1) Offences specified in Part-A of the Schedule; (2) Offences specified in Part-B of the Schedule if the total value involved in such offences is of a particular amount and more; and (3) Offences specified in Part-C of the Schedule.

sentences.text: The offences constituting the complaint for the predicate offence against the petitioners, were under Sections 420, 468, 471 IPC and Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

All those offences which were originally in Part-B of the Schedule before 2015,
have now become Part A of the Schedule.
The petitioners are implicated in 2 out of 5 prosecution complaints in PMLA.
The quantum of proceeds of crime indicated in paragraph 3.12 of the charge-sheet is Rs.17,28,391/- in all the five prosecution complaints in PMLA.

Therefore the contention is that if the prosecution relies upon the merging of the offences under the erstwhile Part-B into Part-A under the Finance Act of 2015, then they must apply the threshold limit which was prescribed originally for Part-B offences.
In view of the said arguable position, we issue notice, returnable in two weeks.

(RADHA SHARMA) (RENU BALA GAMBHIR)
COURT MASTER (SH) COURT MASTER (NSH)
